entities.name: Great Chinese Famine (Great Leap Forward)
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary: The deadliest famine in human history (1959–1961), caused by Mao Zedong's Great Leap Forward policies: forced collectivization, backyard steel furnaces that diverted farm labor, and the suppression of crop failure reports. An estimated 15–55 million died. The disaster led to Mao's partial sidelining and Liu Shaoqi/Deng Xiaoping's pragmatic economic reforms.
